body: ## Impetus 1. \ 2. Demonstrated community interest: from [diffview.nvim](https://github.com/sindrets/diffview.nvim) to [codediff.nvim](https://github.com/esmuellert/codediff.nvim) to [diffs.nvim](https://github.com/barrettruth/forge.nvim), visualizing diffs interactively has only increased in popularity over the last 2+ years 3. Reducing widespread code duplication: _countless_ repositories reimplement the same logic for viewing diffs over and over (I see a new one every week in [r/neovim](https://reddit.com/r/neovim)). This is a good candidate to be "shifted left" into core. ## Goals Improving the visualization of diffs in `filetype=diff` is a small but sensible first step in addressing the points above. - Parse the majority of the [diff specification](https://git-scm.com/docs/diff-format) (recommended to consult during review) - Prettify diff files in a simple, performant, consistent, and readable way - Design should follow the precedent set by other neovim lua plugins such as editorconfig and man ## Previews ### Success Case (Before/After) ### Failed/Missing Parser Highlight Case (Before/After) ## Design Decisions All of these are up to debate - organized here for convenience. | Subject | Decision | Rationale | | --- | --- | --- | | how its exposed | opt-in runtime plugin | not `diffopt`, which is orthogonal (about diff generation, not highlighting) | | name | `diffhl` | n/a | | highlighting | syntax-aware foreground, dimmed background | precedent set by [pierre](https://diffs.com), codex, claude code - more highlighting is needed than simple treesitter fg for the text to stick out as diff added/removed (see [here](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a3314c7f-bf8c-4eb0-b57b-58ef6b8d75c9) for no bg-highlighting) | | how to use it | ftplugin triggered on `filetype=diff` | can be expanded later | | config | `{g,b}:diffhl` | like `editorconfig` | | ft -> language conversion | extract from header and use `vim.filetype.match{filename}` -> `ts.language.get_lang()` | n/a | | Hunk Prefixes | +,>/-,< is add/delete; gracefully fallback otherwise | Match vim syntax file | | Highlight group(s) | text: `@.`; background `Diffhl{Add,Remove}` | n/a | ## Implementation I think it is more useful to describe the core enforced invariants than every detail of the code: **Each hunk is "reconstructed" into real valid source code before parsing.** A hunk interleaves the old and new versions of a file. Every body line with a `+`/`-`/space sigil is obviously invalid. For each hunk the old and new sides are demultiplexed back into two contiguous, separate documents with the sigil stripped. These are parsed after in their corresponding language (indeed, hunks in the same diff may have differing languages). **Rendering costs are a function of the viewport size.** Leveraging ephemeral extmarks, rendering is per-redraw: each redraw the visible rows are recomputed. Off-screen hunks are skipped outright by leveraging binary search on hunks intersecting the viewport. This means that a 10,000-line diff renders like a 50-line one. **(AFAIK) nothing is ever painted stale or wrong.** The parsed hunk list is cached against the buffer's changetick. Each side is parsed once, asynchronously. When a parser may have newly become available (tracked via an autocmd), the cache is invalidated. **Syntax is attempted only on single-column (unified) hunks.** Combined/merge diffs, languages without a TS parser or with an uninstalled TS parsers skip everything. Mapping out the column math is genuinely (more) complex (~30-40 LOC more). ## Prospective Next Steps Some general things of note that I will formalize in issues later, contingent on PR acceptance: - Highlighting [combined/merge diff format](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-diff#_combined_diff_format), which is currently render as plain text. This is less common and requires a more complex implementation. - Expand to `filetype={git,gitcommit}`/provide a mechanism for users to enable this plugin on filetypes - Extensionless filetypes and shebang-based filetypes render as plain text. - Conditionally enabling the plugin on `syntax=treesitter` (? #39009 )

+--- Tree-sitter highlighting of the code inside diff hunks. When attached, every
+--- added/removed line also gets a background tint and a colored +/- marker.
+--- Lines without an available parser keep the tint but receive no syntax highlighting.
+
+local api = vim.api
+local ts = vim.treesitter
+
+local M = {}
+
+local ns = api.nvim_create_namespace('nvim.diffhl')
+
+---@param ft string? the filetype extracted from the hunk header
+---@return string? the treestitter language name, or nil if missing/not installed
+local function resolve_lang(ft)
+  if not ft or ft == '' then
+    return nil
+  end
+  local lang = ts.language.get_lang(ft)
+  if not lang then
+    return nil
+  end
+  local ok, added = pcall(ts.language.add, lang)
+  if ok and added then
+    return lang
+  end
+  return nil
+end
+
+-- Derive hunk treesitter language from header path
+---@param path string
+---@return string?
+local function path_lang(path)
+  if path == '' or path == '/dev/null' then
+    return nil
+  end
+  return resolve_lang(vim.filetype.match({ filename = path }))
+end
+
+--- Normalize a diff header path: strip Git's surrounding quotes (used for
+--- special characters), any trailing "\t<metadata>", and the leading a/ or b/.
+---@param path string
+---@return string
+local function clean_path(path)
+  return (path:gsub('^"(.*)"$', '%1'):gsub('\t.*$', ''):gsub('^[ab]/', ''))
+end
+
+---@class (private) nvim.diffhl.Hunk
+---@field old_lang string?
+---@field new_lang string?
+---@field start integer
+---@field cols integer
+---@field lines string[]
+---@field new nvim.diffhl.Side?
+---@field old nvim.diffhl.Side?
+
+--- Scan {buf} line by line for diff hunks, resolving each hunk's old/new
+--- language from the preceding ---/+++ headers and recording its body lines.
+---@param buf integer
+---@return nvim.diffhl.Hunk[]
+local function parse(buf)
+  local lines = api.nvim_buf_get_lines(buf, 0, -1, false)
+  local hunks = {} ---@type nvim.diffhl.Hunk[]
+  local old_lang = nil ---@type string?
+  local new_lang = nil ---@type string?
+  local hunk = nil ---@type nvim.diffhl.Hunk?
+
+  for i = 1, #lines do
+    local line = lines[i]
+
+    -- Inside a hunk: collect body lines until a line that is not part of the
+    -- body ends it. A "\ No newline at end of file" marker (c == '\\') is
+    -- skipped without ending the hunk.
+    if hunk then
+      local c = line:sub(1, 1)
+      if c == ' ' or c == '+' or c == '-' then
+        hunk.lines[#hunk.lines + 1] = line
+      elseif line == '' then
+        hunk.lines[#hunk.lines + 1] = ' '
+      elseif c ~= '\\' then
+        hunk = nil
+      end
+    end
+
+    -- Between hunks: track the per-file languages from the ---/+++ headers
+    -- (reset at each "diff" line) and open a hunk at each @@/@@@ header.
+    if not hunk then
+      local newf = line:match('^%+%+%+ (.*)$')
+      local oldf = line:match('^%-%-%- (.*)$')
+      if newf then
+        new_lang = path_lang(clean_path(newf))
+      elseif oldf then
+        old_lang = path_lang(clean_path(oldf))
+      elseif line:match('^diff ') then
+        old_lang, new_lang = nil, nil
+      else
+        -- A combined (merge) diff header carries one extra '@' per parent, so
+        -- the number of leading '@' minus one is the count of status columns.
+        -- Hunks are recorded even when the language is unknown so the background
+        -- tint still applies.
+        local at = line:match('^(@@+) %-%d')
+        if at then
+          hunk = {
+            old_lang = old_lang,
+            new_lang = new_lang,
+            start = i,
+            cols = #at - 1,
+            lines = {},
+          }
+          hunks[#hunks + 1] = hunk
+        end
+      end
+    end
+  end
+
+  return hunks
+end

+---@class (private) nvim.diffhl.Side
+---@field lines string[]
+---@field rows table<integer, integer>
+---@field paint table<integer, boolean>
+---@field src string?
+---@field parser vim.treesitter.LanguageTree?
+---@field trees table<integer, TSTree>?
+---@field parsing boolean?
+
+--- Reconstruct the hunk's new and old file contents as separate strings so each
+--- parses as contiguous source. Context lines belong to both sides (so each
+--- parses correctly) but are painted only once, via the new side.
+---@param hunk nvim.diffhl.Hunk
+---@return nvim.diffhl.Side new
+---@return nvim.diffhl.Side old
+local function build_sides(hunk)
+  local new = { lines = {}, rows = {}, paint = {} } ---@type nvim.diffhl.Side
+  local old = { lines = {}, rows = {}, paint = {} } ---@type nvim.diffhl.Side
+
+  for j = 1, #hunk.lines do
+    local line = hunk.lines[j]
+    local c = line:sub(1, 1)
+    local content = line:sub(2)
+    local row = hunk.start + j - 1
+    if c == '+' then
+      local i = #new.lines
+      new.rows[i] = row
+      new.paint[i] = true
+      new.lines[i + 1] = content
+    elseif c == '-' then
+      local i = #old.lines
+      old.rows[i] = row
+      old.paint[i] = true
+      old.lines[i + 1] = content
+    else
+      local ni = #new.lines
+      new.rows[ni] = row
+      new.paint[ni] = true
+      new.lines[ni + 1] = content
+      local oi = #old.lines
+      old.rows[oi] = row
+      old.paint[oi] = false
+      old.lines[oi + 1] = content
+    end
+  end
+
+  return new, old
+end

+--- Parse {side}'s reconstructed source with the {lang} parser once and cache the
+--- trees. If the parse completes asynchronously, request a redraw, but only
+--- while {buf} is still unchanged from {tick}.
+---@param buf integer
+---@param tick integer
+---@param side nvim.diffhl.Side
+---@param lang string
+local function ensure_side_parsed(buf, tick, side, lang)
+  if side.trees or side.parsing then
+    return
+  end
+  if #side.lines == 0 then
+    side.trees = {}
+    return
+  end
+  side.src = table.concat(side.lines, '\n')
+  local ok, parser = pcall(ts.get_string_parser, side.src, lang)
+  if not ok or not parser then
+    side.trees = {}
+    return
+  end
+  side.parser = parser
+  side.parsing = true
+  -- parse() may finish synchronously or hand off to a background job. "sync"
+  -- lets the callback tell the two apart: only an asynchronous completion needs
+  -- to request a redraw, and only while the buffer is still unchanged.
+  local sync = true
+  parser:parse(true, function(_, trees)
+    side.parsing = false
+    side.trees = trees or {}
+    if
+      not sync
+      and trees
+      and api.nvim_buf_is_valid(buf)
+      and api.nvim_buf_get_changedtick(buf) == tick
+    then
+      api.nvim__redraw({ buf = buf, valid = false, flush = false })
+    end
+  end)
+  sync = false
+end
+
+--- Run {fn} for each tree-sitter highlight span on {side} that intersects the
+--- visible rows [{toprow}, {botrow}], passing the buffer row, start/end columns,
+--- and highlight group.
+---@param side nvim.diffhl.Side
+---@param toprow integer
+---@param botrow integer
+---@param fn fun(row: integer, col: integer, end_col: integer, hl: string)
+local function each_span(side, toprow, botrow, fn)
+  if not side.parser or not side.trees then
+    return
+  end
+  local n = #side.lines
+  local first = vim.list.bisect(side.rows, toprow, { lo = 0, hi = n })

comment_data.body:
Based on the previous experience of doing a similar thing, default color scheme should not define highlight groups for plugins (even built-in). It was not met well when I tried to do this for `vim.pack`.

As per groups themselves:
1. If they were to stay, they should be documented along with when they are used.
2. Having a default group hard code colors will introduce a lot of friction for users. Since most of them don't use default color scheme, they'd have to define those themselves or wait for the color scheme upsteam it. Especially since this is (probably) planned to be opt-out and not opt-in.
3. Highlighting whole changed lines with different background *kind of* defeats the purpose of highlighting the code. A lot of color schemes will struggle to find suitable background red and green that would make highlighted code readable on top.

My suggestion and expected behavior of the enhanced highlighting is to highlight only `+` and `-` prefixes with already present `Added` and `Removed` groups. Or maybe even with `@diff.plus` and `@diff.minus`, since this is tree-sitter related. This makes it more usable out of the box and doesn't require adding new highlight groups (both in core and for all color schemes).

Diff patches can have not only `+` and `-` as markers, but arbitrary characters (`--output-indicator-new=<char>, --output-indicator-old=<char>, --output-in‐dicator-context=<char>` parameters of `git diff`).
I am not sure if it is reasonably possible to make this feature work if those markers have changed, but at least making sure that nothing terribly bad happens seems worth it.

Hmm, not sure. IIRC, the diff parser only supports the standard git diffs, not the other formats the legacy syntax supports. I do not know how much of an issue this would be. 

(I also don't know whether the default queries play nice with added/removed highlights on top of syntax, but that could be checked and fixed if necessary.)

I agree that this would be the cleanest solution over DIY injections, but last I looked I was not very happy with the diff grammar -- at least not enough to bundle it. But we could fork (or rebuild from scratch) our own if necessary? (Would need someone interested in writing and helping maintain it.)

There are two separate questions here. 1) Bundling a diff parser could replace some of the hand-written hunk/header scanning; not a blocker for this approach.

2) The part I don’t see how to express with queries **(I am no treesitter wizard)** is the reconstruction step (see bullet 1 in the PR description implementation section). For each hunk we need two virtual sources: `old = context + removed lines + context`, and `new = context + added lines + context`, with marker columns (+,-) stripped and highlights mapped back to the non-contiguous corresponding diff rows. **This is a bare-minimum requirement for syntax-highlighted diffs to look even remotely readable.**

_Can Neovim's current injection & range machinery actually do this?_... express two per-hunk child parses that share overlapping context ranges and may have differing old/new languages?

Obviously, tree-sitter is powerful enough to do this; but I thought injection queries cannot express this?

This approach does not work. The first part makes sense, ts can do that. But the query-to-injection model, AFAIK, cannot work with this. no `injection.combined` = separate parses, no reconstruction allowed (not what we want. `injection.combined` combines matches, but does so _globally_ for the pattern/language (we need it scoped to the hunk). We need a mix of the two.

Perhaps the solution is building and extending nvim's ts injection layer. I'll defer to clason on this.

(Treesitter and diffs are not my strong suits; I can't review)

Edit: Marking this as off-topic as to not take up space.

What about "scoped" injections here? We can use query quantifiers to have a combined tree just for a specific hunk/context section in a diff, i believe. Something like:

```scheme
; addition injection
([
  (context) @injection.content
  (addition) @injection.content
  (deletion)
]+
  ; directives/predicates ...
  )

; same as above but for deletions...
([
  (context) @injection.content
  (addition)
  (deletion) @injection.content
]+
  ; directives/predicates ...
  )
```

so the query runs until it finds a `(block)`, and then stops. But all lines within a chunk should get combined properly. It seems like the kind of problem #34352 was meant to solve
